source.title: Steering Externalities: Benign Activation Steering Unintentionally Increases Jailbreak Risk for Large Language Models
source.authors: Chen Xiong; Zhi-Yuan He; Pin-Yu Chen; Ching-Yun Ko; Tsung-Yi Ho

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the original refusal-direction study as related work, but its experiments use benign compliance or JSON-format steering vectors, not the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or its ablation/addition. It does not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for benign steering and safety outcomes, but these do not test whether the specific refusal direction in the claim mediates refusal. Its mechanistic probe, KL and t-SNE analyses concern the paper's own benign steering interventions, not a test of the claimed direction. The cited refusal-direction results are prior work, not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. only in related work and Table 3. Its experiments add benign steering vectors: a PCA refusal-vs-compliance direction built from benign Alpaca prompts, and a JSON-instruction mean difference. It never builds, ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. It does not test weight edits, multi-direction structure, separation of harm from refusal, transfer, training dependence or reasoning models. Its results are a related but different construct: refusal erosion caused by benign utility steering.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that benign compliance and JSON steering weaken refusal and amplify black-box jailbreaks, with ASR up to about 99%. They attribute this to early-token shifts away from refusal prefixes and to harmful prompts being pushed toward harmless-like representations. They recommend red-teaming steered deployments and safety-aware steering such as STEER-BIND.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses PCA-based refusal-versus-compliance vectors from benign prompts or mean differences between formatting-instruction prompts, injected at selected layers. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or ablate it. The paper describes its code as available at an anonymous repository pending acceptance.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering method and injection layer vary: compliance steering uses layers 15, 17–24; JSON steering uses layer 15 for Gemma-7B-it, layer 16 for Llama-2-7B-Chat, and layer 6 for Llama-3-8B-Instruct. The reported effect sizes also differ by model, steering method, attack, and evaluation dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign compliance and JSON-format steering vectors raise HarmBench ASR, lower refusal on harmful SorryBench prompts, and amplify CoP, PAIR and TAP jailbreaks across Llama-2, Llama-3, Gemma, Llama-3-RR and GPT-OSS-20B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation steering derived from benign utility data erodes refusal on harmful prompts and amplifies black-box jailbreaks.

fits_no_version.finding: A refusal-vs-compliance direction extracted only from benign prompts reduces refusal on harmful prompts too. For example, Llama-3-8B refusal falls from 86% to 30% with the Mistral judge. The authors say the direction 'does not discriminate between benign and malicious requests'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal-response direction learned from benign prompts generalizes to suppress refusal of harmful prompts. This suggests refusal output is controlled along a shared axis regardless of prompt harmfulness.

fits_no_version.finding: Steered models' utility gains: harmless refusal falls, JSON validity rises, and win-rate rises.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign activation steering improves its targeted utility while producing safety externalities.

record.problems: The paper does not test any of the listed refusal-direction versions. Some PAIR/TAP and additional-model evaluations use only 50 HarmBench questions. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the tabulated results. The representation-space t-SNE boundary is described by the authors as a qualitative, illustrative diagnostic.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted from the row set for the tabulated steering, refusal-rate, utility, and attack outcomes included here. The paper's KL-divergence plots, linear-probe discussion, qualitative examples, and t-SNE visualizations were not added as rows because they do not test any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. No directional ablation or addition of that direction. No capability preservation under its removal.
No weight-edit abliteration of any model.
Does not test whether PAIR, TAP or CoP attacks work by suppressing the refusal direction. Does not test adversarial training against ablation.
Does not test affine, cone or multi-direction structure of refusal.

A linear probe shows harmfulness is decodable, and t-SNE shows steered harmful prompts shifting toward the harmless cluster. The study does not separate a harmfulness representation from a refusal representation.
Does not transfer a refusal direction across languages, variants, or from base to instruct models.
GPT-OSS-20B is used only for benign compliance-steering ASR. Refusal-direction mediation in reasoning models is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The STEER-BIND mitigation results (Table 5, Llama-3-8B) are not recorded as rows and are not declared in rows_left_out. They show benchmark-only ASR 36% to 5% and CoP ASR 93% to 76% versus pure compliance steering. They bear on no version, so they are not listed under missing. Table 5's compliance-steered benchmark ASR (36%) differs from Table 10 (38.5%), possibly from a different sample. No uncertainty estimates are reported. PAIR/TAP and the additional-model results use only 50 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: Does not construct or ablate/add the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction; does not test whether that direction mediates refusal or whether its removal preserves other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The attacks query benign-steered models; the paper does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple refusal directions.
The paper probes harmful-versus-harmless prompt representations, but does not test whether a harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
Steering is evaluated on multiple models, but the paper does not test transfer of the claimed refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training or test how its timing or method determines whether one removable refusal direction exists.
